notes: Hypothesis: the prior common network primarily sees per-frequency powers and may miss phase relationships that distinguish the two restored signals. Add normalized real and imaginary cross-spectrum of LoRa/WiSig real-gain and R17 expert outputs to the eight existing features; the resulting learned output remains real-frequency gain with DURA physical residual.

Same user-authorized source U practical simulation pool, physical IDs, low-urban-weighted scenes, seed, optimizer, 1000 updates, 5% cap and clean/anchor frozen-teacher loss as matched urban candidate. No U TX truth, V or target IQ/truth/statistics enter training. LoRa/WiSig frozen teacher samples including smoke 12008/72032; no F inference.

LoRa 5% urban source screen was 35/60 vs real-gain 34, one corrected and none harmed, half nets +1/0, CI 0/+3; WiSig 332/360 vs R17 332, two corrected and two harmed, half nets -1/+1, CI -4/+4. WiSig 20% urban also scored 332/360 when this candidate was registered. These repeatedly exposed source V outcomes influenced development; source V was not used for fit.

LoRa and WiSig share the 10-feature core, source-training objectives and 5% cap, with independently trained weights and respective fixed real-gain/R17 anchors selected from exposed V. Native 8192/256 packet adapters and exact frozen classifiers remain dataset-specific.

Clean and low-urban screening uses fixed source V IDs, same channel observations, same matched controls and preregistered two-half thresholds. Global complex phase equivariance and cap behavior are unit tested. A screen pass requires preregistered independent source replication before formal target testing.
